transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (BlueHarbor Eng Manager), Ravi Patel (Lead ML), Janelle Ortiz (Platform), Tom Brooks (CTO)
Shared links: https://redwood.internal/sdk-snippets (shared by Maya), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pocevidence (customer sheet)

SUMMARY (auto): Quick sync on SDK integration. Main topics - structured output schema, function/tool calling patterns, error handling & retries, benchmark plan.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we will keep to 45, uh, quick agenda - SDK usage, structured output, bench results from last week, and next steps.
[00:12] Sara: thanks, Maya. we have Ravi and Janelle with me. we got the initial integration working but saw some malformed JSON responses when we tried to validate.
[00:20] Diego: okay thanks - that sounds like the structured output constraints weren't enforced. quick Q: are you using the SDK's structured_output parameter or using prompt-level schema?
[00:28] Ravi: we tried both. started with prompt instructions (we put a JSON schema in the system prompt) and then switched to the SDK's structured_output field per the doc, but still see occasional trailing text after the JSON block.
[00:37] Diego: yep, known edge case when streaming partial tokens hit. by default streaming may give you chunked tokens and if your parser is naive it can grab trailing commentary. Did you use the validate_json flag?
[00:48] Ravi: we toggled validate_json on, still saw about 2-3% invalids in a run of 500.
[00:54] Maya: that 2-3% matches what other folks hit when they rely purely on soft constraints. we recommend using the SDK's structured schema enforcement plus a small post-parse validator: if the parser sees trailing tokens, toss and re-request with the same conversation + prompt-suffix - there are idempotent retry patterns in the draft runbook.
[01:11] Tom: is that retry going to blow up costs? we are sensitive to token billing.
[01:15] Maya: good point. Diego, can you explain the retry/backoff guidance?
[01:18] Diego: sure. pragmatic approach: 1 immediate retry with stricter schema enforcement (set deterministic:true on the call if available), if still invalid then run a short transform that extracts the JSON block by looking for first/last braces and then validate - that costs a tiny bit extra but keeps overall re-requests low. Also batching reduces per-request overhead. For our hosted mode, retries are cheap relative to spinning up additional capacity. For Dedicated, you may want to tune batch sizes to reduce token emission variance.
[01:43] Sara: what about function/tool calling? our app uses a legal-check tool (internal microservice) and a DB lookup tool for meta-data. we want the model to call the tool only when confidence high. how do we wire that with the SDK?
[01:56] Diego: the SDK supports tool definitions - you register a function signature and a JSON schema for the tool's input. the model returns a tool invocation payload, e.g., {"name":"db_lookup","arguments":{"id":"1234"}} and the SDK will call your tool adapter. you can set a confidence threshold on the SE side (we added a plugin for thresholding) or implement minimal post-filtering.
[02:13] Ravi: any sample snippet?
[02:15] Maya: shared in the chat - link: https://redwood.internal/sdk-snippets - but quick pseudo: redwood.client.call({ model, tools: [db_lookup], structured_output: {schema: mySchema}, streaming: true, deterministic: false }) - then the callback receives tool calls and you decide to execute.
[02:32] Janelle: does the SDK guarantee that tool call arguments match the JSON schema? we saw decimals as strings sometimes.
[02:38] Diego: SDK will try to coerce where sensible but doesn't mutate types silently; it validates and will surface a validation error. If you set strict_schema:true, the SDK returns an error rather than coerced value. For numerics it's best to annotate the schema explicitly and add sample values in function docstrings.
[02:55] Tom: do we need to host the tool router on a separate endpoint? what's the latency impact if the model triggers multiple tool calls per request?
[03:04] Diego: tool calls are sync by default in the SDK flow - the model emits a tool invocation, you run it, return the result, then the model continues. Each tool adds round-trip latency. Our recommendation: 1) collapse lookups into batched tool calls, 2) prefetch likely entries using prefix caching, or 3) move small microservices co-located with the inference layer (in Dedicated or Private deployments) to reduce RT.
[03:28] Sara: about caching - does Redwood maintain a KV cache that you can plug into? we have a lot of small user-profile lookups.
[03:35] Diego: yes, we have automatic KV prefix caching for session tokens and recently accessed keys, but currently the SDK exposes a hooks API for prefetch and cache hints. For Private customers we can enable co-located Redis and give you a connector. Janelle, that dovetails with your VPC questions.
[03:49] Janelle: right, we need to confirm outbound network egress. our infra team needs to know IP ranges and ports.
[03:55] Maya: noted - action item: I'll send the security brief and the VPC egress ranges (see next steps).
[04:00] Ravi: switching to perf - we ran a 500-run test last week. median was ~210ms but 95th was 430ms on hosted, with small variance depending on model (we used rwd-medium). can Dedicated help us hit 95th < 350ms?
[04:15] Diego: yes, Dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized kernels reduces 95th substantially, but depends on sequence length and batching. If your average seq len is small (<256 tokens) we can optimize kernel selection and reach the target. Also quantized variants of the model can reduce latency at mild quality tradeoffs.
[04:33] Ravi: what's the effort to switch from hosted to dedicated mid-POC?
[04:37] Maya: we can do a hybrid - start hosted for dev, then schedule a Dedicated pilot for a week to run your exact workload; Diego can help run the pilot and match kernel/configs. usually a 2-3 day setup to provision capacity and configure routing.
[04:50] Tom: security checklist - SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO. are those available for POC?
[04:56] Maya: yes, we have a SOC2 summary and KMS options for Private/Dedicated. for hosted POC we can enable audit logs retention and SSO test accounts; I'll include the addendum in the docs we send.
[05:06] Sara: one more - structured output validation: does Redwood support schema-specific scoring so we can track regressions?
[05:13] Diego: Redwood Optimize can tie structured output to evals; you upload a golden dataset and it reports accuracy over time, with alerts on regressions. for POC, we can run nightly evals on your sample set.
[05:23] Ravi: minor note - we saw model occasionally prefer a different tool name (db_lookup_v2 vs db_lookup) - is there name aliasing?
[05:30] Diego: yes, define aliases in the tool table. the model sometimes uses the nearest alias. enforce strict names or provide alias list to reduce confusion.
[05:37] Maya: ok let's recap next steps. we'll share updated SDK snippet and a short runbook for retries and streaming edge cases. you'll run a 2k-benchmark and we will provision a Dedicated trial if results indicate it's valuable.
[05:48] Sara: good. thanks. any blockers from your side?
[05:51] Ravi: network egress detail and a patched SDK snippet that uses strict_schema + deterministic on retries.
[05:57] Maya: noted, will do.
[06:00] Tom: thanks everyone.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

NOTES: occasional mis-transcriptions: "deterministic" heard as "deterministric" in a few spots; model names sometimes transcribed as rwd-med rather than rwd-medium.

References in call: SDK snippet link (internal), POC benchmark sheet (customer drive).
